s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis
salient_findings: Heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus with solid and cystic components
Erosion of orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
key_facts: Teenage girl presented with several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
External deviation of her nasal septum for several weeks
No significant past medical history
Left nasal mass noted on examination
Mild left-sided proptosis present
CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
Displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved
Bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
Biopsy results showed spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells
Rare mitotic activity and no cytologic atypia

differentials: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus
per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus

shortlist.label: Central Giant Cell Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis, and biopsy results showing spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with biopsy results showing significant multinucleated giant cells, although less common in this age group and location

shortlist.label: Ossifying Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the clinical presentation and imaging findings of a heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus, but less likely than Central Giant Cell Granuloma given the biopsy results

shortlist.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Although a possible cause of nasal obstruction and facial swelling, the biopsy results and imaging findings are not typical for this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the imaging findings of a heterogeneous mass with bony changes, but the biopsy results are not consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus with spindle cell process and significant multinucleated giant cells, along with rare mitotic activity and no cytologic atypia, is consistent with Central Giant Cell Granuloma. The age of the patient and the location of the mass also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
rejected.why: Typically occurs in older adults and has more aggressive features

rejected.label: Ossifying Fibroma
rejected.why: Usually has a more uniform appearance on imaging and lacks significant multinucleated giant cells

rejected.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
rejected.why: Typically occurs in males and has a more vascular appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Usually has a more ground-glass appearance on imaging and lacks significant multinucleated giant cells
